## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
This maintenance visit recorded a critical deficiency in pump operation. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its nameplate current, indicating no hydraulic load. This is a failure condition requiring immediate professional attention. All other system components measured within normal parameters.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3.0 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8.0 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48.0 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The liquid level is at the outlet. The effluent filter was cleaned during this maintenance visit and measured in good condition with light soiling.

## PUMP OPERATION
| Parameter | Measured | Nameplate | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amp Draw | 1.6 A | 7.2 A | CRITICAL - No Load |

The pump is energized and running, but the measured current draw of 1.6 amperes is only 22.2% of the nameplate rating. This indicates the pump is operating without hydraulic load -- the motor is spinning but no fluid is being moved. The combination of low amp draw and confirmed pump operation points to one of three failure modes: the impeller is broken or missing, the discharge line is severed or disconnected, or the pump is running dry. Any of these conditions will cause rapid motor overheating and failure if operation continues.

The high water alarm tested functional. Electrical connections are sound.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
The dispersal field surface is dry with no evidence of breakout or ponding.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE PRIORITY:**
- **Immediate professional attention required.** The pump is operating at no load. A qualified technician must examine the impeller, check the discharge line for disconnection or blockage, and verify that fluid is actually leaving the pump. Do not continue operating the system in this condition; motor damage from dry-run operation will occur rapidly.

**SECONDARY:**
- Once pump operation is restored, recommend a follow-up maintenance visit within 30 days to confirm normal amp draw and verify that the aerobic treatment unit is functioning properly.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### Pump Operation
The pump that moves treated water from the tank to the dispersal field is not working correctly. It is running, but it is not moving water. This is a serious problem because the motor will overheat and fail within hours or days of continued operation. The system cannot disperse treated effluent while the pump is not functioning, which means untreated wastewater will back up into the tank and eventually into your home.

Do not ignore this finding. Contact a qualified septic technician immediately to diagnose and repair the pump.

### Tank Solids
This maintenance visit recorded solids at approximately 23 percent of tank volume, which is within the normal range. Continue managing the system by keeping non-biodegradable material out -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease, and medications all damage the biological treatment process and accelerate solids accumulation.
